findings.title: CVE-2026-19868 - NVD entry
findings.summary_md: NVD published the CVE-2026-19868 entry on 6 November 2026 with SonicWall PSIRT as the source, describing an authentication enforcement flaw in the SonicOS SSL-VPN service. The entry notes that a user with valid credentials for an alternate authentication method may bypass SAML authentication controls, including SAML-enforced MFA, and CISA marks exploitation as active. SonicWall's advisory identifier is SNWLID-2026-0014.

findings.title: SonicWall CVE-2026-19868: SAML MFA Bypass, Check And Patch
findings.summary_md: Ciphers Security published a detailed guide stating that CVE-2026-19868 affects SonicOS Gen7 builds 7.3.3-7015 and older and Gen8 builds 8.2.2-8015 and older, with fixes in 7.3.4-7013 and 8.2.3-8015 respectively. The post states SonicWall reports no workaround, that only SSL-VPN with SAML enabled is affected, and that six other CVEs are fixed in the same release. It also provides a hunt using SonicOS event ID 1080 SSL-VPN logins correlated with identity-provider sign-ins, since no vendor IoCs exist.

findings.title: CISA Flags SonicWall SonicOS MFA Bypass Flaw Amid Reports of Possible Exploitation
findings.summary_md: The Hacker News reported that CISA added CVE-2026-19868 to the KEV catalog following reports of possible exploitation, and that SonicWall's Friday advisory acknowledged investigating a report of potential exploitation. The article cites CVSS scores of 7.1 (SonicWall) and 7.5 (CISA enrichment) and notes additional patched flaws including CVE-2026-107155 and CVE-2026-107154. SonicWall did not share details on the attacks or threat actors.

findings.title: Exploited SonicWall SSL-VPN flaw lets attackers bypass SAML-enforced MFA (CVE-2026-19868)
findings.summary_md: Help Net Security reported that CVE-2026-19868 is an authentication enforcement flaw in the SonicOS SSL-VPN service exploitable only when SAML is enabled for SSL-VPN logins, and that the flaw was discovered and reported by Ryan Harris of IT services provider Electronic Office. The article notes no workarounds are listed and the same releases fix six other vulnerabilities. It states attackers need working credentials first, but SAML-enforced MFA is the control the flaw can bypass.

findings.title: SonicWall SSLVPN Authentication Bypass Added to CISA KEV
findings.summary_md: eSecurity Planet reported that CISA added CVE-2026-19868 to the KEV catalog on 6 November 2026 with a remediation deadline of 20 November 2026 for federal civilian agencies. The article lists affected Gen7 builds of SonicOS 7.3.3-7015 and earlier and Gen8 builds of 8.2.2-8015 and earlier, with fixes in 7.3.4-7013 and 8.2.3-8015. It stresses the flaw is an authentication enforcement issue requiring valid credentials for an alternate method, not an unauthenticated bypass.

findings.title: SonicWall SSL VPN Flaw Lets Attackers Bypass MFA - And It's Being Exploited
findings.summary_md: IT-Connect reported that SonicWall PSIRT investigated a report indicating potential exploitation of CVE-2026-19868 and urged customers to upgrade, and that CISA added the flaw to KEV the same day, confirming active exploitation. The article notes the flaw affects only SSL-VPN where SAML is enabled and carries a CVSS score of 7.1. It describes the bypass as requiring valid credentials for another authentication method.
